source.title: Algorithmic Task Capture, Computational Complexity, and Inductive Bias of Infinite Transformers

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates length adaptation on a task designed to require induction-style token copying, but does not identify or intervene on induction heads.
record.gate_note: The study reports an induction-task adaptation result in Fig. 1(a). It does not report induction-head measurements or training-time formation/loss-curve results. Values in the figure are not numerically stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study uses an induction-style copy task as one benchmark for its 'algorithmic capture' criterion, which tracks adaptation cost as sequence length grows. It never identifies, ablates or tracks attention heads, previous-token composition, formation timing, or in-context-learning loss. Its result shows that a 2-layer model's task solution extrapolates with roughly logarithmic extra samples. That does not bear on whether any version holds, so this is not a test (T4: the finding serves as a task within the authors' own framework).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors report evidence of capture on the induction task, alongside sorting and string matching. They attribute this to the tasks' low EPTHS complexity. They draw no conclusion about induction-head formation or mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a task-level length-adaptation and sample-budget criterion rather than identifying or measuring attention heads or their formation.

fits_no_version.finding: A 2-layer, 4-head causal transformer with RoPE (base 500,000), trained on an induction copy task at T0=50, extrapolates to T=10,000. The extra samples needed grow roughly logarithmically in T, consistently across 5 seeds (Fig. 1a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformers that learn an induction-style copy task length-extrapolate with only logarithmic sample re-adaptation (algorithmic capture).

record.problems: The induction result is shown in a figure without numerical values in the text. It measures task-level adaptation, not induction-head presence or causal role; the reported induction experiment uses one stated architecture and setup.

untested.parts: No head identification, previous-token composition, or attention-pattern evidence; only task-level adaptation cost.
No training-time formation, phase change or loss-bump measurement.
No large-model ICL or token-index loss analysis.
No cross-family, size or architecture comparison of induction heads.
No manipulation of data or training that is linked to induction-head formation.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites De Luca et al. as reporting poor OOD performance on induction-head-style tasks; that is a cited result, not a row. App. A describes the theoretical architecture as having no causal masking or residuals, while the induction experiment uses a standard causal transformer. The theory therefore does not directly describe the experimental model.

versions.untested_parts: Tests the induction-style sequence-completion task, but does not establish that heads form, compose with previous-token heads, or implement the behavior by attention.
No induction-head formation timing, in-context-learning phase change, or training-loss bump is measured.
No large-transformer in-context-learning loss-by-token-index measurement or estimate of induction heads' contribution to most ICL.
No cross-family, size, run, architecture, or modality comparison of induction heads.
No comparison of how data or training setup affects induction-head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
No few-shot task-learning or alternative-head/mechanism comparison.
No measurement of separate formation sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: Causal Transformer (Induction)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the induction task at base length, then incrementally adapted to larger sequence lengths.
rows.measure: Relative adaptation cost (P/P0) as sequence length increases
rows.baseline: Initial training budget P0 at T0 = 50; numerical value not stated
rows.uncertainty: One STD error bars; numeric values not stated
rows.note: The authors describe capture consistent across seeds. This reports task-level induction-style completion/adaptation, not whether induction heads formed or carried out the behavior.
rows.check: Measures relative adaptation cost (P/P0) for length extrapolation on an induction-style task. This is a task-level capture measure, not induction-head presence, mechanism (V1) or formation dynamics (V2/V7). Values are figure-only. The record's V1 link should be removed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
